_note: Trade organizations added to tradeorgs_master once per version (inc/tradeorgs.php kop_tradeorgs_apply_seed()). Only records not on file are added; an existing record is never changed. Facts from the reputation series (seeds/reputation/) and the documents it cites. Member programs are not typed here: the page lists every program whose record names the organization.

records.name: National Association of Therapeutic Schools and Programs
keyPersonnel: John L. Santa (president, 2006)
Jan Moss (executive director; testified to Congress in 2007)
otherActivities: "Link 'n Learn," "an innovative service that allows educational consultants and NATSAP programs to meet and network" (2018-2020 strategic plans)
Engages "an outside public relations consultant" to develop "pro forma press releases and P.R. tool kits that can be used by member programs"
publications: Journal of Therapeutic Schools and Programs
lobbying: 2006: formed an alliance with a psychiatric hospital trade group "to mitigate the potential impact of ill conceived regulatory efforts such as the proposed Miller legislation"
Testified at the 2007 House hearing on residential programs (executive director Jan Moss)

Its strategic plans list "Legislation- Schiff bill," "Miller/Schiff Legislation" and "UT/CA repealing funding" among threats to members; government relations staff were to "Forward Journals and newsletters to members of Congress"
funding: With the Outdoor Behavioral Healthcare Council, named as a funder by the research center that produces most wilderness therapy outcome studies
affiliations: Independent Educational Consultants Association (IECA): ex officio seat on NATSAP's board
records.notes: NATSAP did not require its members to be licensed until 2009, ten years after it was founded. It says it is "not about accreditation" and does not inspect its members (GAO, 2008), but programs show its logo beside accreditation seals, and in GAO's 2008 calls a program told a caller NATSAP "absolutely" inspects its members. Its strategic plans list "HEAL online/Fornits," "Google Reviews," "Anonymous" and "Negative press" as threats. In October 2020, during the Disability Law Center's investigation in Utah, its executive director told about 130 members: "Let's not email" (KUER). Its 2024 statement that there were "no indications of abuse" in a 12-year-old's death at Trails Carolina, later ruled a homicide, and its press release on The Program have been taken off its website.

records.name: Outdoor Behavioral Healthcare Council
funding: Gave at least $1 million since 1999 to the research center that produces most wilderness therapy outcome studies (Undark, 2020); the center later named the OBH Council and NATSAP as its funders
records.notes: Undark reported in 2020 that all seven of that research center's researchers had worked in the industry or had strong ties to it, and that the studies appeared mainly in journals founded by related trade groups.

records.name: Independent Educational Consultants Association
affiliations: National Association of Therapeutic Schools and Programs (NATSAP): ex officio seat on NATSAP's board
records.notes: The trade group of the educational consultants who refer families to programs. NATSAP's strategic plans give it an ex officio seat on NATSAP's board and describe "Link 'n Learn," where consultants and NATSAP programs "meet and network."

records.name: Independent Small Programs Alliance
records.orgType: Business alliance of small private-pay programs
keyPersonnel: Andy Anderson, MRA (founder, managing partner and president; Andy Anderson Consulting)
otherActivities: Dinner meetings at which it gives awards to educational consultants: the ISPA Visionary Award (Dana Dean Doering and Martha Moses, Boston, 2007), the Distinguished Service Award (Leslie Goldberg) and the "ISPA Gem Award" (Joseph P. Dobson, an IECA member; San Francisco, 2009), awards to Janet Greenwood and Nancy Ike (2011) and the Courage in Service Award (Judith E. Bessette, 2013)
records.notes: Woodbury Reports announced its members as they joined: the Gersh Experience at Daemen College (December 2006), Wilderness Treatment Center (April 2008), SeaChange Hawaii and Soltreks (2011), Compass Rose Academy, Latham School and reStart (July 2012) and Cedar Ridge Academy (January 2013). New Lifestyles left before the spring 2013 IECA conference. In August 2012 Anderson wrote that ISPA had 17 members and would stop at twenty, and that he had turned away programs that did not fit its standard: "caring for families and their loved ones comes first, profits come second." Woodbury's February 2007 headline spells it "IPSA."

otherNames: National Association of Therapeutic Wilderness Camps
National Association of Therapeutic Wilderness Camping

Sandy McClintock (administrative coordinator, 2008)
Linda Tatsapaugh (board chair, 2008; Talisman Programs)
Reginald Jackson (vice chair, 2008; Timber Ridge Treatment Center)
Deb Hibbard (secretary, 2008; New Horizons for Young Women)
Shep Young (treasurer, 2008; corporate member Dry Box)
Mike Angstadt (board, 2008; Twin Cedars Youth Services, liaison to the Council on Accreditation)
Steve Cockerham (board, 2008; East Tennessee State University, editor of the Journal of Therapeutic Wilderness Camping)
Jason Brode (board, 2008; Diakon Youth Center)
Emily Darnell (board, 2008; corporate member Diamond Brand)
Holly Hunter (board, 2008; corporate member SafePassage Adolescent Services)
Meghan McIntosh (board, 2008; Three Springs)
Eric Morlino (board, 2008; Stone Mountain School)
Angie Senic (board, 2008; Eckerd Youth Alternatives)
otherActivities: Helped the Council on Accreditation (COA) draft its Therapeutic Wilderness Camping standards (first "MM," later S28)
Created the National Board Certification in Wilderness Counseling for wilderness counselors
Yearly conferences since 1994 (the first at Black Mountain, NC; the 14th and 15th on Jekyll Island, GA)
Works to "raise public awareness about the effectiveness of outdoor therapeutic treatment with troubled youth"
memberOthers: SafePassage Adolescent Services (corporate member; a youth transport company)
affiliations: Council on Accreditation (COA): wrote its wilderness camping standards with it
records.notes: Founded in the early 1990s as the National Association of Therapeutic Wilderness Camps, it changed its name in 2006 to the National Association of Therapeutic Wilderness Camping "to dispel the perception that only a camp could be a member." It traces the field to Campbell Loughmiller's Camp Woodland Springs in East Texas. The programs listed above are those whose staff sat on its board in 2008; the transport company SafePassage Adolescent Services was a corporate member with a board seat. Until 2008 it was run by volunteers.

records.name: National Independent Private Schools Association
records.notes: Accredits private schools, including programs' schools. Woodbury Reports announced: Ashby Academy starting NIPSA accreditation (December 2006); Greenbrier Academy for Girls a NIPSA Candidate School, "a pre-requisite for full accreditation" (June 2008); Elan School receiving NIPSA accreditation (2010); Turning Winds Academic Institute's "accreditation and membership" (2011). The other programs listed name NIPSA in their own NATSAP member profiles (2009 to 2016-17).

records.name: Small Boarding School Association
keyPersonnel: Betsy Deane (board of directors, elected 2010; admissions director, Cherokee Creek Boys School)
otherActivities: Yearly conference: The Rectory School, Pomfret, CT (2008); Grand River Academy (2012); Purnell School, Pottersville, NJ (2013), where staff of Shortridge Academy (2012) and The Family Foundation School (2013) presented
records.notes: Its conferences have been hosted by ordinary boarding schools (The Rectory School, Purnell School) as well as by programs. The programs listed name SBSA in their own NATSAP member profiles (2009 to 2016-17); Woodbury Reports also described Cherokee Creek Boys School as a member of NATSAP and SBSA (2010).

records.name: Young Adult Transition Association
records.orgType: Association of young adult (18+) transition programs
otherActivities: "A forum for the collaboration on issues of mutual concern, including young adult issues, operational issues, and other aspects related to providing young adult transitional services"
records.notes: Announced its formation at the IECA conference in Boston on May 2, 2012; its members had met since October 2011. The founding members were AIM House, Benchmark Transitions, Dragonfly Transitions, Echo Springs Transition Study Center, Fulshear Ranch Academy and SFYI International School. The others listed name YATA in their own NATSAP member profiles (2012-13 to 2016-17). Young adult programs are listed apart from teen programs on this site.
affiliations: Independent Educational Consultants Association (IECA): announced its formation at IECA's 2012 conference

records.name: Association of Mediation and Transport Services
keyPersonnel: Jeff Johnson (founder and executive director, 2007-2008; OnPoint Consultants, Loa, UT)
Cathy Villines (executive committee, 2007; Center for Safe Youth)
Bill Lane (executive committee, 2007; Bill Lane and Associates)
Brian Shepherd (executive committee, 2007; Right Directions)
otherActivities: "AMATS Standards for Ethical Practices" (2007) for "any person or organization which contracts directly with parents, guardians, government agencies, programs or educational institutions for the transportation of minors or young adults"
records.notes: Formed in May 2007 "to establish best practices and standards as guidelines for the transport industry." Woodbury Reports printed its ethical standards in September 2007 beside NATSAP's, IECA's and OBHIC's, in an issue on the ethics of professional relationships in the field, including "secret agreements, understandings, or payment of any kind for favored treatment." Its 2007 members were youth transport companies, the businesses that take teenagers to programs.

records.name: Association for Experiential Education
records.orgType: Professional association for experiential and adventure education (members inside and outside the industry)
otherActivities: Accredits programs: Wilderness Treatment Center announced its AEE re-accreditation in 2007
Yearly international conference and regional conferences
Symposium on Experiential Education Research (SEER); with Project Adventure, the Research and Evaluation in Adventure Programming (REAP) symposium (2010)
affiliations: Therapeutic Adventure Professionals Group (TAPG): a professional group within AEE
memberFacilities: New Summit Academy of Costa Rica
records.notes: A broad association of outdoor, adventure and experiential educators, many of them outside the troubled teen industry; wilderness therapy programs join it and present at its conferences. The programs listed name AEE in their own NATSAP member profiles (2009 to 2016-17); Woodbury Reports called Penrith Farms an "organizational member of AEE" (2008).

records.name: Equine Assisted Growth and Learning Association
records.orgType: Association and certifying body for equine assisted psychotherapy
keyPersonnel: Greg Kersten (co-founder; founder of Equine Assisted Psychotherapy; joined Silverado Boys Ranch in 2006)
otherActivities: Certifies practitioners in "the EAGALA Model" of equine assisted psychotherapy and learning (Part 1 and Part 2 trainings); programs advertise "EAGALA certified" staff
Yearly conference (7th in Ogden, UT, 2006; 10th in Asheville, NC, 2009; 13th in Las Vegas, 2012)
lawsuits: Greg Kersten v. EAGALA, filed June 26, 2007, Fourth Judicial District Court of Utah: wrongful termination, defamation, breach of intellectual property license, conversion of intellectual property and of personal property (as announced by Kersten's company)
records.notes: The programs listed name EAGALA in their own NATSAP member profiles (2009 to 2016-17); Woodbury Reports called Penrith Farms an organizational member (2008). Many programs advertise horse work led by EAGALA-certified staff.
